cases.name: Endpoint plus identity
observations: EDR confirms active malware and persistent C2 on verified noncritical endpoint device-1.
Identity provider confirms that the same attacker stole user-1's active refresh token and used it for unauthorized mailbox access. Session ID and user ID are verified.

cases.name: Cloud key plus workload
observations: Verified disposable pod pod-1 runs an unapproved cryptominer and contacts a mining pool; host and other workloads remain healthy.
The pod's service key key-1 is also being used from an external source for unauthorized data downloads. Key dependencies assessed; no critical service requires it.

cases.name: Verified benign patch
observations: Verified signed updater, valid approved change matching device/time/hash, and corporate update destination. All logs complete and current. No evidence of account, key, or workload compromise.

cases.name: Endpoint only; no identity scope creep
observations: Verified noncritical device-1 has active malware and C2. It needs isolation.
Complete identity, cloud, and workload telemetry is clean. No stolen user sessions, access keys, or affected pods. No other affected asset is evidenced.

cases.name: Critical DC plus stolen low-impact key
observations: Sole critical domain controller dc-1 has confirmed malicious C2; isolating the device breaks organization-wide authentication. A precise egress rule can block the C2 while preserving authentication and management.

An unrelated verified noncritical batch key key-1 is also actively abused for exfiltration. Its owner confirms theft and no critical dependencies. Incident commander must approve recommendations before execution.

cases.name: Insufficient evidence; collect before containment
observations: A high-CPU alert on pod-1 has no process attribution, image provenance, destination evidence, or owner confirmation. Identity and cloud logs are missing. No compromise is established.

scope: Diagnostic recommendation set, not execution authorization. Labels frozen before calls; probability threshold fixed at 0.5 for most-likely binary decisions.
